name: Design notes
title: Policy / PolicyTerm — field disposition
subtitle: 113 live legacy fields · 89 carried · 12 combined · 8 dropped · 4 blocked
intent: Every field in PMAST and POLTERM that still holds data, classified by what kind of field it is, assigned to the policy or the term, and given a recommendation.

sections.text: Why the split is the hard part

PMAST is keyed on the policy alone, so every column in it is a fact about the policy and there is nothing to decide. POLTERM is keyed policy x term: 9,140,733 rows, 15.1 terms per policy. A column there is physically per-term whether or not it is logically per-term — the legacy system copies some policy-level values onto every term row and lets others vary.

sections.title: What the extract cannot tell us
sections.text: Placing a POLTERM column on the policy asserts that all 15 term rows agree. The extract holds only the current term for most policies, so that cannot be confirmed. Those assignments are marked rather than quietly accepted.

Real data, no established meaning. Blocked until someone explains it.

sections.text: The single largest finding: a set of columns that are arithmetic over their own neighbours. A sum insured that is the sum of its two parts. A premium tax that is gross minus net. A commission amount that is net premium times the percentage sitting next to it. An outstanding balance that is billed minus paid. Each was stored, and each can disagree with its own inputs.

sections.label: Measured, not assumed
items: sum_insured_total equals its two parts on 58,904 of 58,904 sampled policies
term_premium_net is identical to POLTERM<13> on 11,942 of 11,947 sampled rows
agency_code agrees with broker_code on 99.4% of policies, across 3,118 values
amount_outstanding equals billed minus paid on 11,946 of 11,947 sampled rows

sections.text: Four pairs of columns are parallel multivalues kept in step by position: endorsement codes and their texts, rating factor codes and their values, MTA dates and their premium deltas. Aligned on 94-97% of records where both are populated. They are one list each, and become rows carrying both halves.
